title: Grounds for processing
summary: Process digital personal data only for a lawful purpose with the data principal's consent or for a listed legitimate use.
typical_evidence: Records of processing showing purpose and lawful ground for each activity

title: Notice
summary: Give each data principal a clear notice of the personal data collected and the purpose; how to withdraw consent and exercise rights; how to complain to the Board.
typical_evidence: Privacy notice; notice shown at collection; notice in English and Eighth Schedule languages where offered

title: Consent
summary: Consent must be free specific informed unconditional and unambiguous with clear affirmative action; limited to necessary data; as easy to withdraw as to give.
typical_evidence: Consent capture flow; consent records with timestamp and purpose; withdrawal flow

title: Consent managers
summary: Where a registered consent manager is used the fiduciary accepts consent and withdrawal through it.
typical_evidence: Consent manager integration and agreement (only if used)

title: Certain legitimate uses
summary: Processing without consent is limited to the uses listed in the Act such as data voluntarily provided for a specified purpose; employment; legal obligations; emergencies.
typical_evidence: Legitimate use analysis per processing activity

title: Accountability of the data fiduciary
summary: The fiduciary is responsible for compliance including processing done by its processors.
typical_evidence: Privacy programme ownership; DPDP compliance plan

title: Engaging data processors
summary: Engage processors only under a valid contract.
typical_evidence: Processor inventory; DPAs with each processor

title: Accuracy and completeness
summary: Ensure accuracy completeness and consistency where data is used for decisions about the principal or disclosed to another fiduciary.
typical_evidence: Data quality and correction procedures

title: Technical and organisational measures
summary: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to comply with the Act and Rules.
typical_evidence: Security and privacy policies; control implementation evidence

title: Reasonable security safeguards
summary: Protect personal data in possession or control including with processors by reasonable security safeguards to prevent breach.
typical_evidence: Encryption; access control; logging and monitoring; backups (see DPDP-R6)

title: Personal data breach intimation
summary: Inform the Data Protection Board and each affected data principal of a personal data breach.
typical_evidence: Breach response procedure; breach register; notification templates (see DPDP-R7)

title: Erasure and retention
summary: Erase personal data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served unless law requires retention; make processors erase too.
typical_evidence: Retention schedule; deletion jobs; processor deletion confirmations

title: Published contact
summary: Publish business contact information of the DPO or a person who can answer questions about processing.
typical_evidence: Privacy notice and website showing contact details

title: Grievance redressal
summary: Establish an effective mechanism to redress data principals' grievances.
typical_evidence: Grievance procedure; grievance log with response times

title: Children and persons with disability
summary: Obtain verifiable consent of a parent or lawful guardian; do not process in ways likely to harm a child; no tracking behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising at children.
typical_evidence: Age gating; verifiable parental consent flow; ad targeting exclusions (only if children's data processed)

title: Significant data fiduciary obligations
summary: If notified as a significant data fiduciary appoint a DPO based in India; appoint an independent data auditor; run DPIAs and periodic audits.
typical_evidence: SDF notification assessment; DPO appointment; DPIA; independent audit report (only if notified)

title: Right to access information
summary: On request provide a summary of personal data processed; processing activities; and the identities of fiduciaries and processors it was shared with.
typical_evidence: Access request procedure; sample responses

title: Right to correction and erasure
summary: On request correct complete update or erase personal data subject to retention required by law.
typical_evidence: Correction and erasure procedure; DSR tickets

title: Right of grievance redressal
summary: Data principals can raise grievances with the fiduciary which must respond within the prescribed time.
typical_evidence: Grievance channel; response timeline records

title: Right to nominate
summary: Data principals can nominate another person to exercise their rights in case of death or incapacity.
typical_evidence: Nomination mechanism

title: Transfer outside India
summary: Transfers outside India are allowed except to countries restricted by government notification; sector rules may be stricter.
typical_evidence: Data residency map; transfer inventory; check against restricted list and sector rules (RBI etc.)

title: Exemptions
summary: Record any exemption relied on (e.g. legal claims; research; certain startups as notified) and its basis.
typical_evidence: Exemption analysis (only if relied on)

title: Notice contents and form
summary: The notice must be standalone and clear with an itemised description of data and purposes and a link to withdraw consent and exercise rights.
typical_evidence: Notice review against Rule 3 contents

title: Consent manager registration and duties
summary: Consent managers must be registered and meet the conditions in the Rules.
typical_evidence: Only if the company is or uses a consent manager

title: Reasonable security safeguards (minimum)
summary: Minimum safeguards include encryption obfuscation or masking; access control; logs and monitoring to detect unauthorised access; backups for continuity; log retention for at least one year; and processor contracts with safeguards.
typical_evidence: Encryption settings; IAM exports; audit log config with at least 1-year retention; backup plans; DPAs

title: Breach intimation timelines
summary: Inform affected principals without delay in plain language; inform the Board without delay and give a detailed report within 72 hours of becoming aware (or longer if the Board allows).
typical_evidence: Breach procedure with 72-hour clock; notification templates; breach register

title: Erasure timelines for specified fiduciaries
summary: Specified classes of fiduciaries must erase data after the prescribed period of inactivity and warn the principal at least 48 hours before erasure; retain processing logs for at least one year.
typical_evidence: Inactivity deletion job; pre-erasure notice; log retention (only if in a specified class)

title: Contact information of DPO or responsible person
summary: Prominently publish contact details of the DPO or responsible person on the website or app and in responses.
typical_evidence: Website or app screenshot; response templates

title: Verifiable consent for children
summary: Use reliable identity and age details or a virtual token to verify the parent or guardian before processing a child's data.
typical_evidence: Parental verification flow (only if children's data processed)

title: Additional obligations of significant data fiduciaries
summary: Annual DPIA and audit; due diligence on algorithms; any data localisation the government specifies.
typical_evidence: Only if notified as SDF

title: Exercising rights and response timelines
summary: Publish how to make rights requests and respond to grievances within the prescribed period (up to 90 days).
typical_evidence: Rights request page; DSR log with response dates

title: Cross-border transfer requirements
summary: Meet any requirements the government sets for making data available to foreign states or entities.
typical_evidence: Transfer inventory; contractual safeguards
